config.prompt: Two systems, opposite physics — file each trait under the half it describes:

items.label: municipal pressure of roughly 250–500 kPa does the work
pipes run small, sealed, sized by flow demand
runs at carefully chosen slopes, sized generously

a fault blocks, gurgles, and lets sewer gas into living space

activities.caption: rebuild the chain from cholera to code
activities.name: plumbCholeraOrder

config.prompt: How a code section becomes a memorialised outbreak — assemble the chain:
items: Crowded industrial cities draw drinking water from rivers they also foul with sewage
1854: John Snow maps cholera deaths around London's Broad Street pump and traces the outbreak to a contaminated well
Water source separation is demonstrated to save lives — epidemiology's founding moment
Indoor plumbing, water treatment and building codes spread together, and the diseases retreat from the cities that adopt them
config.why: Each step forced the next — which is why every code section a plumber follows today can be read as a memorialised outbreak.

activities.caption: walk the trench-side decisions before anyone digs
activities.name: plumbTrenchBranch

config.root: You are the site lead for a morning of dig work. Walk the decisions in order.

start.text: The dig will pass 1.8 m deep. What is decided first?

choices.label: Classify the soil, then plan a protective system
Start digging — a morning job does not need shoring

protect.text: Soil classified before entry; trenches over about 1.5 m get sloping, shoring or a trench box. Next call:

choices.label: Park the spoil pile right at the edge for easy access
Spoil back from the edge, ladders within reach

spoil.text: A spoil pile at the edge adds surcharge to the very wall you are protecting — it goes back from the edge.

choices.label: Set the site up properly instead

site.text: Spoil back, ladders within lateral reach, protective system in before entry. The trench is now a workplace rather than a trap.

collapse.text: An unsupported trench can bury a worker under a cubic metre or more of soil — more than anyone can dig out in time. There is no fast version of this rescue.

choices.label: Back up and set protection first

config.why: Trenching is the trade's deadliest hazard, and the defence is a sequence, not a single rule: classify soil, protect over 1.5 m, spoil back, ladders in reach.

activities.anchor: torches have started fatal building fires
activities.caption: one line of this safety briefing is wrong — click it
activities.name: plumbTorchSpot

config.prompt: One line of this student's safety briefing is wrong — click it:
lines: Soldering copper demands flame-resistant shields and cleared combustibles around the joint.
Water at 60 °C can cause a serious burn in seconds, so heaters are tempered and anti-scald valves guard tubs and showers.
Manholes and pits can hold bad air or hydrogen sulphide — confined-space rules apply.
GFCI protection for power tools in wet environments is optional if the extension cord looks undamaged.
Cast iron fittings and water heaters punish bad lifting form — lifting discipline is part of the hazard map.
config.correction: GFCI protection in wet environments is mandatory practice, not a cord-appearance judgement call.
config.why: Electricity plus wet surroundings is a fixed pair in this trade — the protection is required equipment, exactly like gloves or shields.

activities.caption: pair each backflow term with its job
activities.name: plumbBackflowMatch

config.prompt: Backflow prevention in five pieces — pair each with its work:

pairs.right: any link between potable water and a contamination source
the water-main break or firefighting draw that turns the link into a straw
the simplest prevention — an unbridgeable vertical break
the testable device certified testers check periodically

config.why: The invisible hazard is a two-part event — a link plus a pressure drop — and each device removes one of the two parts.

activities.anchor: Drainage relies on gravity, so slope is everything
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the code's working band for slope
activities.name: plumbSlopeCloze

config.text: Common horizontal drains run at about %%0%% to %%1%% per cent; the classic residential figure is a quarter-inch of fall per foot, roughly %%2%% per cent. Too flat and solids %%3%%; too steep and liquids %%4%% them, stranding the heavy material.
config.hint: Two ends of the code band, its classic midpoint, and the two verbs for what goes wrong on either side.

activities.anchor: a steeper drain always drains better
activities.caption: mark the classic residential target on the slope scale
activities.name: plumbSlopePlace

config.prompt: Mark the classic residential drainage target on the slope scale (per cent):
config.why: A quarter-inch of fall per foot is roughly 2 per cent — inside the 1–4 per cent band. Past the band, liquids outrun the solids and strand the heavy material along the pipe.
